title: FastAPI Security Handbook: OAuth2, JWT, Scopes, CORS & API Keys
summary: Quick revision notes on securing a FastAPI app: the OAuth2 password flow, signed JWT access tokens, password hashing, security dependencies with scopes, CORS middleware and API keys.

chapters.title: Security Mental Model
points: Authentication = who are you (401 Unauthorized); authorization = what may you do (403 Forbidden)
OAuth2 password flow: client POSTs username + password as form data to a token endpoint and receives an access token, then sends it as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' on every request
Server stays stateless: the signed JWT carries the identity, so no session lookup is needed per request
FastAPI security classes (OAuth2PasswordBearer, APIKeyHeader) are declared as dependencies and also add the Authorize button to the OpenAPI /docs page
Password flow suits only first-party clients you fully trust; third-party apps should use authorization code flow with PKCE

chapters.title: Password Hashing
points: Never store plaintext or fast hashes (MD5, SHA-256 alone); use a slow, salted algorithm such as bcrypt or argon2
Hashing is one-way: you never decrypt, you re-hash the login attempt and verify it against the stored hash
Salt is generated per password and embedded in the hash string, so identical passwords produce different hashes
Example with pwdlib: PasswordHash.recommended(); hash = ph.hash(pw); ph.verify(pw, hash)
Mistake: comparing hashes with == (use the library verify, which is constant-time) or returning 'user not found' vs 'wrong password' as different errors (user enumeration)

chapters.title: JWT Access Tokens and the Login Endpoint
points: JWT = header.payload.signature, each base64url-encoded; the payload is readable by anyone, only signed (not encrypted), so never put secrets in it
Standard claims: sub (subject/user id), exp (expiry, Unix time), iat (issued at); add scopes as a custom 'scope' claim
Create: jwt.encode({'sub': user, 'exp': now + timedelta(minutes=30)}, SECRET_KEY, algorithm='HS256'); decode: jwt.decode(token, SECRET_KEY, algorithms=['HS256'])
Login route: @app.post('/token') takes form: OAuth2PasswordRequestForm = Depends(), verifies the user, returns {'access_token': jwt, 'token_type': 'bearer'}
Mistakes: hardcoded SECRET_KEY (generate with openssl rand -hex 32, load from env), no exp, omitting algorithms= on decode (allows algorithm confusion), and long-lived tokens with no refresh strategy

chapters.title: Security Dependencies and Scopes
points: oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl='token') extracts the bearer token from the Authorization header and returns 401 if missing
get_current_user(token = Depends(oauth2_scheme)) decodes the JWT, loads the user and raises HTTPException(401, headers={'WWW-Authenticate': 'Bearer'}) on failure
Chain dependencies: get_current_active_user depends on get_current_user and raises 400/403 for disabled users; routes just declare Depends(get_current_active_user)

Scopes: OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl='token', scopes={'items:read': '...'}); guard routes with Security(get_current_user, scopes=['items:read']) and check SecurityScopes.scopes against the token's scope claim
Mistakes: trusting scopes the client requested without limiting them to what the user is allowed, and using Depends instead of Security when the route needs scopes

chapters.title: CORS Middleware and API Keys
points: CORS is a browser rule: a page from one origin (scheme+host+port) cannot read responses from another unless the server allows it; it does not protect your API from curl or other servers
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=['https://app.example.com'], allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=['*'], allow_headers=['*'])
Preflight: browsers send an OPTIONS request with Access-Control-Request-* headers for non-simple requests (custom headers, JSON, PUT/DELETE); the middleware answers it automatically

Never combine allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=True: Starlette then mirrors any caller's Origin on preflight and responses, so any site can make credentialed calls; list explicit origins instead

API keys: APIKeyHeader(name='X-API-Key', auto_error=False) as a dependency; compare with secrets.compare_digest, store only hashed keys, and use keys for server-to-server access while JWT bearer tokens serve user sessions

chapters.title: Security Cheat Sheet
points: Login flow: POST /token (form) -> verify hash -> issue JWT -> client sends Authorization: Bearer <jwt> -> Depends(oauth2_scheme) -> decode -> user
Status codes: 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer for bad or missing credentials; 403 for authenticated but not allowed (missing scope)
Hash: pwdlib/argon2 or bcrypt, never MD5 or SHA alone; JWT: set exp, pin algorithms=[...], keep SECRET_KEY in env (openssl rand -hex 32)
Dependency choice: Depends(oauth2_scheme) for the token, Security(dep, scopes=[...]) for scoped routes, APIKeyHeader for service keys
CORS checklist: explicit origins, no '*' with credentials, add middleware once, and remember it is browser-only protection
